steps.verify: the state text pinned in the file (the md5 of each of the 22 function definitions and the trigger text, enabled); owner, privileges, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path and volatility of the five replaced functions unchanged; no client role may execute a server-only function (all checked inside the file)
steps.what: One policy owner (fn_personal_memory_policy_v1 = the pause); the writers return a real status and write nothing; a trigger on public.agent_user_memory refuses every other writer with an error; fn_raziel_context returns an empty personal context without a verified consent and never in a group; export and erasure of memory without deleting the account. Research (round 9): research is written and may be read during the pause only when the RECORD AND ITS CONTENT are positively attested - an approval of an existing row, bound by a fingerprint to the content that was approved, or a record that is wholly canonical Tanakh text - and carry no personal detail (a veto). A matching title, a source string a writer declares, and the absence of a match to the personal-detail filter prove nothing. research_output_write is enforced by the writer function and the trigger, direct writes included. Erasure (round 9): the permission to use research is not the classification for deletion. The default erasure removes personal memory only; a neutral research-typed row stays, approved or not, unless the person asks for research too. Profile facts have their own key (write_profile_facts): a consent to memory does not open them (D-CL13-3).
steps.preflight: Fail-closed: the file continues only when the state is exactly the live 12.11.2026 state or exactly the applied state. Also stops when public.tanach_verses (the canonical text that attests a quotation) is missing.

missing_decisions.what: Edge first for all six functions (kept) or the database step first, alone.

How research becomes usable during the pause: an approval act on an existing row, which binds its content (the trigger supports it; no administrative function performs it yet), or a record that is wholly canonical text. Until rows are approved NOTHING is research: the reader returns no research without the person's consent. Approving the existing 72 rows that come from imported method documents would be a separate data change with its own approval; it is not in this file.

Whether the default erasure should also remove research-typed rows that carry no pattern-detectable personal detail. Today it does not (round 9); a personal statement that no pattern sees, inside a research-typed row, is removed only when the person asks for research too.
May an administrator view stored profile facts during the pause. Blocks closing CL-13, not this step.

research_eligibility.rule: A research-typed row of a research bot (hatishbi: research_note, uriel: method_discovery) is research output only if (1) its record AND content are attested by ONE of: approval (status approved / canonical, set by an UPDATE of an existing row; the trigger writes a binding = the fingerprint of the title, the content and data at that moment; any later change of that content voids it; an INSERT can never claim it) or verse (the title, the content and every string inside data are each a quotation of at least 8 letters from one verse of public.tanach_verses, and at least one is non-empty; the technical key subtype is ignored) AND (2) title, content and data carry no personal detail (a veto, never a proof).
not_a_proof: the absence of a match to the personal-detail filter
a title that matches the canonical text over an arbitrary body
a source string a writer declares (p_source / source)

codex_cases.verse_analysis: A1: the record that is wholly the verse and its analysis title is stored and returned.
codex_cases.title_over_personal_body: A3c, A5a: 'analysis of the verse ...' over 'I was fired yesterday and cannot pay the rent' is refused in the content and in data, by the writer function and by a direct write; the detector sees nothing in that body (Q5).

research_eligibility.research_output_write: Enforced in fn_mem_add and in the trigger, direct writes and edits included (A7-A7d). Without the grant and without the consent of that person the row is refused; with the consent it is stored as that person's own memory.
research_eligibility.effect_on_live_rows: Read-only 13.11.2026: 383 research-typed rows (hatishbi 159, uriel 224). None is approved and none carries a binding, so none is research after this file: the reader withholds all of them without the person's consent. The default erasure would remove the 11 that a pattern marks as personal (birth 5, family 2, health 4) and keep the other 372.
research_eligibility.effect_on_the_bots: During the pause a bot stores a finding only if the whole record is canonical text. A finding with an interpretation, or extracted from a conversation, is not stored. Both bots are dormant (no cron).
limits: Free analysis text is never attested by the canonical-text route; it needs an approval.
No approval act exists yet: nothing sets status approved except a direct SQL change that is separately approved.
An approval or an edit made by a writer who holds the service key is not distinguishable from an act of ZURIEL: the Human Gate is procedural, not cryptographic.
The detector is a pattern list and sees only what it lists.

erase_semantics.permission_to_use_vs_classification_for_: The first is fn_personal_memory_row_is_research_v1 (attested and free of a personal detail). The second is only: not a research type of a research bot, or a personal detail in it. The lack of an approval to read research is not a decision to delete it.
default_erasure_removes: every row that is not a research type of a research bot (conversations, questions, preferences, profile facts, and research-typed rows of the assistant)
a research-typed row that carries a personal detail by the patterns
default_erasure_keeps: research-typed rows of research bots without a pattern-detectable personal detail, approved or not (counted as kept_research_output)
erase_semantics.explicit_option: p_include_research_output = true removes every research-typed row as well.
erase_semantics.export: kind = research_output (attested, no detail) / research_unapproved (research type, no detail, not attested: may not be used during the pause) / personal_memory (everything else).
